The practical issue, of course, will depend in part on how "sideways unstable" f modes of 1.4 M☉ neutron stars do get enhanced, while the full sausage mode does not. Perhaps 1.45 or 1.455 M☉ compact stars would better achieve linear amplification, while still remaining a bit more compact than a main-sequence star proper. 

An important consideration is that neutron stars are orbited by their binary companion. I think, critically, that this brings neutron stars closer together in compactness and binary orbital paths in non-circularity.
